concept: A banner is a message placed on a pane: its tone is shown by a bar, an icon and words, and it arrives the way objects settle.

default_to_avoid.pattern: start-edge accent stripe, tinted icon disc, bold title over muted body, a box inside the pane (Carbon inline notification, Material banner, every admin template)
default_to_avoid.why_not: it treats a floating pane as a page and the message as a form error, adds a second surface inside one sheet of glass, and paints the tone in colour the scene should own

derivation.consequence: a soft shadow below and a rim of light on the top-left edge say where the pane floats
derivation.form: a message that needs attention is its own object with its own shadow and rim, placed relative to the pane it is about

derivation.consequence: panes enter by rising a short distance and settling, as an object placed in space would
derivation.form: the message arrives by rising a few pixels and settling instead of fading in place

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns almost no colour of its own
derivation.form: no tinted fill or stripe; the tone colour appears only on a small glyph

derivation.consequence: status is spoken in text as well as shown in colour
derivation.form: each tone has its own glyph shape and the tone is spoken as a word before the message

derivation.consequence: the loud action sits apart from secondary ones, never between them
derivation.form: a message action sits at the far end of the message, never inline with the pane own actions

root.why: the banner body sits in a measured well that keeps body text above 4.5 to 1 over bright photos

icon.why: a tone disc with an icon gives a second, non-colour cue for the kind of message

info.why: information tone maps the bar and disc to the accent pair

positive.why: success tone maps the bar and disc to the green status pair

warning.why: warning tone maps the bar and disc to the amber pair with ink on the disc

critical.why: error tone maps the bar and disc to the red status pair

body.why: title and detail stack as one reading block next to the icon, so the message reads top to bottom

title.why: the title is the only semibold text in the banner so the message is caught in one glance

detail.why: detail text uses the measured secondary colour so it reads below the title in rank

action.why: an optional action sits apart at the end so it never competes with the pane loud action

sr.why: a visually hidden prefix speaks the tone, such as Warning, because the bar colour is not read aloud

dismiss.why: the dismiss control is a quiet disc with a 44px press area around it, named after what it closes

hover.why: hovering dismiss brightens its icon to the primary text colour, answering the pointer quietly

focus-visible.why: keyboard focus draws the shared ring with its halo so the focused control is visible on any scene

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours drop glass and fills, so a real system-colour border is drawn to keep the shape visible

color.why: the dismiss icon colour eases at hover pace so the change reads as a response

@banner-in.why: a new banner drops a few pixels into place and settles, so a message arriving is noticed without a flash
